cards.title: Sea Otters Keep a Favorite Rock in Their Armpit Pouch
cards.body: Sea otters love eating hard-shelled sea urchins and clams, but they do not crack them open with their teeth. Instead, they store a favorite anvil stone in a loose pocket of skin under their forelegs. They carry this preferred rock on multiple diving trips, resting it on their chests while floating on their backs to hammer open their catch.

cards.title: Female Dragonflies Fake Their Own Death to Avoid Males
cards.body: Courting can be exhausting for female moorland hawker dragonflies. When pursued by overeager males after mating, a female will suddenly freeze in mid-air, crash to the ground, and lie completely motionless. Believing she is dead, the aggressive pursuer flies away. Once the coast is clear, the female simply gets up and flies off to lay her eggs in peace.

cards.title: Hagfish Slime Expands 10,000 Times in Volume in Milliseconds
cards.body: When a predator bites a hagfish, the creature releases a cloud of mucus proteins from its skin glands. Within a fraction of a second, this protein reacts with seawater to expand over 10,000 times in volume. The sudden surge of thick, sticky slime clogs the attacker's mouth and gills, forcing the predator to choke and release the hagfish unharmed.

cards.title: Male Nursery Web Spiders Give Fake Presents to Mates
cards.body: Male nursery web spiders secure mating opportunities by presenting females with a gift of food wrapped neatly in silk. However, lazy or hungry males frequently cheat. They wrap up empty seed husks, plant twigs, or already-eaten insect exoskeletons instead. By the time the female uncovers the trick, the male has already mated and fled to safety.

cards.title: A Swiss Factory Malfunction Once Made It Rain Chocolate
cards.body: In August 2020, residents of Olten, Switzerland, noticed a mysterious brown dust falling from the sky. A minor ventilation malfunction at a local Lindt & Sprüngli factory had blown finely crushed cocoa nibs into the air. Strong summer winds carried the cocoa particles across town, dusting cars and streets in a thin, fragrant layer of real chocolate snow.

cards.title: Sarcastic Fringehead Fish Fight by Mouth-Wrestling
cards.body: The sarcastic fringehead is a ferocious ocean fish known for extreme territoriality. When two rivals compete for a shelter like an empty clam shell, they engage in dramatic open-mouth duels. Unfurling massive, brightly colored membranes around their jaws, they press their mouths directly together like a strange kiss to determine which fish has the larger, more intimidating gape.

cards.title: Pistol Shrimp Snap Bubbles That Reach 4,000 Kelvin
cards.body: The tiny pistol shrimp hunts by snapping its specialized claw at extreme speeds. This movement shoots out a jet of water that generates a collapsing cavitation bubble. When the bubble implodes, temperatures inside briefly exceed 4,000 kelvin—nearly as hot as the surface of the Sun—and produce a loud acoustic shockwave that instantly stuns prey.

cards.title: Sloths Lose Up to 30 Percent of Their Weight in One Poop
cards.body: Sloths have an incredibly sluggish metabolism, taking up to a month to digest a single meal. Because of this, they only defecate about once a week. When they finally descend to the forest floor, they eliminate so much built-up waste at once that they can lose up to 30 percent of their total body weight in a single bowel movement.

cards.title: The Binturong Smells Exactly Like Hot Buttered Popcorn
cards.body: The binturong, a mammal native to Southeast Asian forests, carries an unmistakable movie-theater scent. Its urine contains 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline, the exact chemical compound formed during the Maillard reaction when corn kernels pop. As the binturong drags its tail and scent glands across tree branches to mark territory, it leaves behind a rich aroma of fresh popcorn.

cards.title: Goldfish Do Not Have a Three-Second Memory Span
cards.body: Contrary to popular belief, goldfish do not forget everything every three seconds. Scientific experiments show that goldfish retain memories for months. They can be trained to respond to light cues, navigate complex underwater mazes, recognize individual human faces, and remember feeding schedules. Their long-term memory capabilities match those of many birds and mammals.

quizzes.question: Where do sea otters store their favorite anvil rocks when diving?
options: In a skin pouch under their forelegs
Inside their mouth pouches
Tucked into their tail fur
In seaweed nests on the surface
quizzes.explanation: Sea otters have a loose pocket of skin under their forelegs where they store their favorite cracking stone.

quizzes.question: Why do female moorland hawker dragonflies crash to the ground and lie motionless?
options: To regulate their body temperature
To avoid unwanted courtship from males
To trick underwater fish into surfacing
To molt their exoskeleton safely
quizzes.explanation: Female moorland hawker dragonflies fake their own death to discourage persistent male suitors after mating.

quizzes.question: How does hagfish slime defend against attacking predators?
options: It burns the predator's skin with acid
It expands rapidly to clog the attacker's gills
It numbs the predator's jaw muscles
It creates a dark cloud that hides the hagfish
quizzes.explanation: Hagfish slime expands over 10,000 times in seawater, clogging the attacker's mouth and gills with gel.

quizzes.question: What do some male nursery web spiders do to avoid catching real food for females?
options: They offer shiny pebbles instead
They wrap up empty seed husks or twigs in silk
They steal prey directly from web nets
They sing ultrasonic vibrations instead of giving gifts
quizzes.explanation: Lazy male nursery web spiders wrap up worthless twigs or empty seed husks in silk to trick females into mating.

quizzes.question: What caused a town in Switzerland to be dusted in real cocoa powder in 2020?
options: A controlled agricultural aerosol test
A local bakery explosion
A ventilation malfunction at a Lindt factory
A rare weather phenomenon carrying dust from West Africa
quizzes.explanation: A ventilation failure at a Lindt chocolate factory in Olten blew fine cocoa nib dust across the town.

quizzes.question: How do sarcastic fringeheads resolve territorial disputes over shelters?
options: They perform complex side-to-side dances
They press their massive, fully opened mouths together
They change skin colors to match the substrate
They slap each other using their pectoral fins
quizzes.explanation: Sarcastic fringeheads engage in mouth-wrestling matches, pressing open jaws together to compare mouth size.

quizzes.question: What creates the extreme heat generated by a pistol shrimp's claw snap?
options: Friction from specialized scales
A collapsing cavitation bubble
An electrical discharge between claws
A chemical reaction from internal glands
quizzes.explanation: The high-speed jet of water forms a cavitation bubble whose rapid collapse generates extreme heat and sound.

options: Multiple times per day
Once every day at dusk
About once a week
Only once per season
quizzes.explanation: Sloths have very slow digestion and usually only descend to the ground to poop about once a week.

options: 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline
Sodium bicarbonate
Isoamyl acetate
Capsaicin
quizzes.explanation: Binturong urine contains 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline, the exact chemical created when corn kernels pop.

quizzes.question: What have scientific studies revealed about goldfish memory?
options: It resets every three seconds
It lasts for months and supports complex learning
It is only active while feeding
It only functions in salt water
quizzes.explanation: Experiments show goldfish retain memories for months, learn mazes, and recognize human faces.

misconceptions.claim: Goldfish have a memory span of only three seconds.
misconceptions.explanation: Goldfish retain memories for months, remember feeding routines, and can navigate complex mazes.

misconceptions.claim: Male nursery web spiders only present genuine edible insects as courtship gifts.
misconceptions.explanation: Lazy males frequently wrap worthless twigs or empty seed husks in silk to trick females into mating.

misconceptions.claim: Sea otters must find a new rock every time they dive because they cannot carry tools while swimming.
misconceptions.explanation: Sea otters store their preferred cracking rock in a skin pouch under their forelegs across multiple dives.

misconceptions.claim: Female moorland hawker dragonflies will crash to the ground and play dead to avoid persistent males.
misconceptions.explanation: Female moorland hawker dragonflies intentionally freeze and drop out of the air to escape male harassment.
